questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a trading account?

options.text: To calculate the net profit of a business.
To determine the gross profit of a business.
To prepare the statement of financial position.

questions.explanation: The primary purpose of a trading account is to determine the gross profit by comparing sales with the cost of goods sold.

distractorRationale.a: Net profit is calculated in the profit and loss account, not the trading account.
distractorRationale.c: Recording transactions is the purpose of journals and ledgers.
distractorRationale.d: The statement of financial position is a separate financial statement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is added to purchases when calculating the cost of sales?
questions.explanation: Carriage inwards is added to purchases as it represents the cost of bringing goods to the business.

distractorRationale.a: Returns inwards reduce sales, not purchases.
distractorRationale.c: Closing inventory is subtracted from the cost of sales.
distractorRationale.d: Sales revenue is not part of the cost of sales calculation.

questions.stem: If a business has a high gross-profit margin, what does this indicate?

options.text: The business has high operating expenses.
The business is efficient in controlling its cost of sales.
The business has low sales revenue.
The business has a high level of debt.

questions.explanation: A high gross-profit margin indicates that the business is efficient in controlling its cost of sales relative to its sales.

distractorRationale.a: Operating expenses affect net profit, not gross profit.
distractorRationale.c: Low sales revenue would typically reduce the gross-profit margin.
distractorRationale.d: Debt levels are not directly related to gross-profit margin.

questions.stem: Returns outwards decrease the cost of sales.
questions.explanation: Returns outwards, or purchase returns, decrease the cost of sales as they reduce the total purchases.

questions.stem: Explain how closing inventory affects the calculation of gross profit in a trading account.
markingGuide: Closing inventory is subtracted from the cost of sales.
It represents unsold goods at the end of the period.
A higher closing inventory reduces the cost of sales, increasing gross profit.
questions.explanation: Closing inventory is the value of goods unsold at the end of the period and is subtracted from the cost of sales to determine the cost of goods sold.
